Final ALLFRAME+TRIAL solution from 7 of 11 Cepheids with P>20 d; shorter-period stars were excluded for incompleteness. Hill et al. calibration and R_V=3.3 were adopted. No metallicity correction enters this modulus.

Alternative solution obtained by applying the standard Key Project PL fit to the original Tanvir et al. photometry. It uses seven long-period Cepheids and is not the paper's preferred ALLFRAME distance.
They calculate gamma.

Uncorrected re-fit of seven previously selected Cepheids using the Stetson WFPC2 zero point, Udalski OGLE-LMC PL relations and mu_LMC=18.45. The error is the internal R_PL term; no galaxy-specific systematic error is tabulated.
HST V,I data originally from Tanvir et al. and reanalyzed by the Key Project. The quoted error is random only. A common LMC zero-point uncertainty of about 0.2 mag is discussed but not included.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Preferred OGLE+10 Wesenheit solution before the +0.07 mag metallicity correction. It uses 64 visually selected high-quality ACS Cepheids; the 0.05 mag error also spans analysis choices.
Final ALLFRAME+TRIAL fit to 17 of 36 Cepheids with P>25 d. Dust, bright background and anomalous aperture corrections motivated a 0.15 mag photometric random term, producing the relatively large e_R.

Alternative Key Project fit to Saha et al. photometry. Four outliers were removed from their 25-star final set, leaving 21 Cepheids; the unweighted mean of the individual dereddened moduli was adopted.
There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.

Uncorrected re-fit of 17 previously selected Cepheids using the Stetson WFPC2 zero point, Udalski OGLE-LMC PL relations and mu_LMC=18.45. The quoted error is internal; the paper does not assign a galaxy-specific systematic term.

Published Sandage/Saha HST photometry reanalyzed by the Key Project is refitted with the OGLE-LMC PL calibration. The random error includes PL scatter and reddening uncertainty; no metallicity correction is applied.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Udalski et al. (1999) PL calibration shifted to mu_LMC=18.50. This solution is 0.12 mag shorter than the MF91 result and differs from the value adopted by Freedman et al. (2001).
Preferred modulus, obtained as a conservative average of the MF91 and Udalski solutions. The uncertainty was enlarged accordingly; no separate systematic error or metallicity correction is provided.
Madore & Freedman (1991) PL calibration. The error is mainly associated with observational scatter. Photometry is fainter than earlier reductions, likely because of the local-sky treatment.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution used as a consistency check. CTE corrected; no metallicity correction.
Representative mean-light result using the authors' OGLE LMC PL fit. CTE corrected but not metallicity corrected; the error is random only.

There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.
Uncorrected re-fit of nine previously selected Cepheids on the Stetson and Udalski OGLE-LMC calibration. The value is referenced to mu_LMC=18.45; only the internal random R_PL uncertainty is listed.
The relatively large random uncertainty reflects the small 11-Cepheid sample and reddening-error propagation. The shared LMC zero-point systematic is not included in the tabulated modulus error.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Representative mean-light OGLE LMC solution. CTE corrected but not metallicity corrected; random error only.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution. It agrees exactly, to the quoted precision, with the mean-light LMC result.

HST/WFPC2 used 17 F555W and 4 F814W epochs. Although 95 bona fide Cepheids were catalogued, the adopted modulus uses 45 with logP>1.25, 0.60<(V-I)<1.10 and Q>=4. A +0.05 mag long/short-exposure correction was applied. No metallicity correction; aperture and zero-point systematics were discussed but not separately quantified.

Alternative Key Project fit to the original Saha et al. photometry, using the article's stated 44-Cepheid P>18 d sample. This shorter cutoff is more susceptible to incompleteness than the preferred P>25 d fit.

Final ALLFRAME+TRIAL solution from 51 of 94 Cepheids with P>25 d, selected to reduce incompleteness bias. It agrees with the earlier Saha et al. distance; no metallicity correction enters the tabulated modulus.
There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.

WFC-only true modulus from 45 Cepheids. The PC-WFC difference is +0.031+/-0.113 mag, consistent with zero and smaller than the +0.11 mag severe-blending prediction. No metallicity correction was applied.

PC-only true modulus from six Cepheids, calculated as part of the blending test. It is not the paper's adopted global distance to NGC 4496A. The quoted uncertainty is internal and no systematic term is tabulated.

Uncorrected re-fit of 51 previously selected Cepheids using the Stetson WFPC2 zero point and Udalski OGLE-LMC PL relations. The listed uncertainty is the internal R_PL term; systematic components are discussed but not assigned individually.
The largest sample among these hosts gives a small random error. Sandage/Saha HST data reanalyzed by the Key Project are fitted with OGLE-LMC slopes. LMC zero-point systematics are excluded.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Representative mean-light OGLE LMC solution. Includes the +0.05 mag STS CTE correction but no metallicity correction.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution. CTE corrected and consistent with the corresponding mean-light result.
There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.
Key Project HST V,I photometry is refitted with fixed OGLE-LMC PL relations. The reported uncertainty is random and includes PL scatter plus reddening coupling; no metallicity term is used.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution. It is 0.018 mag shorter than the representative mean-light value.
Representative mean-light OGLE LMC solution. CTE corrected but not metallicity corrected.
Alternative fit to Saha et al. photometry using 17 high-quality Cepheids on chips 1, 3 and 4. Chip 2 was excluded because its modulus was 0.66 mag larger; including it would give mu0=31.03+/-0.11.

Final ALLFRAME+TRIAL solution. The PL fit uses 27 of 39 candidates with P>20 d to limit incompleteness. All four WFPC2 chips are included because this reduction shows no significant chip-dependent offset.
There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.

PC-only true modulus from six Cepheids, derived for the differential blending test. It is a chip-specific PL result rather than an adopted global galaxy distance. The quoted uncertainty is internal; no separate systematic term is provided.
WFC-only true modulus from 21 Cepheids. Its offset from the PC result is -0.035+/-0.167 mag, inconsistent with the +0.11 mag shift predicted by severe blending. No metallicity correction was applied.
Uncorrected re-fit of 27 previously selected Cepheids using the Stetson WFPC2 zero point, Udalski OGLE-LMC PL relations and mu_LMC=18.45. Only the internal random R_PL uncertainty is tabulated.

Sandage/Saha HST observations reanalyzed by the Key Project are used. The fit solves simultaneously for distance and reddening. The quoted error is random; the dominant common LMC systematic is omitted.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Representative LMC mean-light solution. Includes the +0.05 mag STS CTE correction; random error only.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution used as a consistency test. CTE corrected without metallicity correction.
Re-fit of published Gibson et al. (2000) WFPC2 photometry using the OGLE+10 PL relations. The number of retained Cepheids is not stated clearly; the +0.08 mag metallicity correction is not applied.
There are no specific comments on the publication. Cepheid moduli are compiled and homogenized from earlier HST Key Project and independent studies. Previous author included it.
The random error is enlarged by the modest Cepheid sample and propagation of the reddening estimate. The modulus assumes mu_LMC=18.50 mag and excludes the common zero-point systematic.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Maximum-light LMC PL solution. It is nearly identical to the corresponding mean-light result.

LMC-calibrated alternative without metallicity correction. It is 0.147+/-0.060 mag below the cited SH0ES value and is considered less suitable because of the LMC-NGC 5584 metallicity mismatch.
